content.title: Asymmetric Scale Exchange | Continuous Evasion in Shared Space
content.summary: In the continuous shots that do not cut off the spatial relationship, the giant body is allowed to occupy the space with slow and heavy committed movements, while the small body moves sideways, bends and circles through the negative space in sequence; both sides can always be positioned, and the ending retains a continuous confrontation rather than a fictional victory or defeat.

quick_start.input_format: Two bodies with clear size and scale + Shared ground + Giant body committed to action + Small body with visible route changes + Shared final state without fictional victory or defeat
quick_start.recommended_input: The handheld inspection vehicle passed through three marked passages at the Mingliang Paper Factory, and the giant crane slowly swept across the space. The inspection vehicle only passed by waiting, changing lines, and lowering the sensing pole. At the end, both sides kept running and did not declare victory or defeat.
required_anchors: Establish the full scale difference and a common ground plane before the first exchange.
Give the large body one slow committed movement that visibly occupies a route.
Preserve both participants and the ground axis through each recovery.
Hold the final shared state without inventing defeat, rescue or alliance.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: In the continuous shots that do not cut off the spatial relationship, the giant body is allowed to occupy the space with slow and heavy committed movements, while the small body moves sideways, bends and circles through the negative space in sequence; both sides can always be positioned, and the ending retains a continuous confrontation rather than a fictional victory or defeat.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: An asymmetric-scale exchange is readable when one large body repeatedly commits slow, space-consuming movements and a smaller body answers with precise route changes through visible negative space. Continuous shared geography, not impact spectacle, proves the tactical relationship, and the ending must not claim a victory the image does not show.

invariants.rule: Establish the full scale difference and a common ground plane before the first exchange.
invariants.purpose: Lets viewers judge mass and available space.
invariants.ablation_failure: Tight fragments hide the central asymmetry.

invariants.rule: Give the large body one slow committed movement that visibly occupies a route.
invariants.ablation_failure: Random flailing produces noise instead of pressure.

invariants.rule: Answer with a smaller subject's route change through a visible gap rather than equal-force collision.
invariants.purpose: Makes agility, not implausible strength, the counter-rule.
invariants.ablation_failure: A head-on match erases the scale premise.

invariants.rule: Preserve both participants and the ground axis through each recovery.
invariants.ablation_failure: Reframing either participant out breaks the exchange logic.

invariants.rule: Hold the final shared state without inventing defeat, rescue or alliance.
invariants.ablation_failure: An unsupported win condition overstates the visible ending.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: source body proportions and attack choreography

instantiations.concept: A palm-sized inspection rover crosses a bright paper mill floor while a slow overhead bale arm sweeps across marked lanes. The rover waits, slips through a visible gap, pivots under a second sweep and ends facing the still-active arm in one continuous lateral shot.
